goal: Upgrade Kimi Code Agent from a native CLI wrapper into a complete macOS coding-agent workbench with trustworthy diff review, parallel task orchestration, and automatic browser/test verification
description: The current SwiftUI app streams Kimi output and persists tasks, but it still has three major gaps versus mature coding-agent desktop products: no structured diff review, no multi-agent/worktree orchestration, and no end-to-end verification loop. The design must preserve local-first execution, explicit user approval, low UI latency, and a native macOS experience.
tasks: Capture structured file, command, test, permission, and lifecycle events from Kimi Runtime
Build a native diff review center with file tree, split/unified diff, line comments, accept/reject, and continue-task actions
Create a supervisor orchestrator that decomposes tasks into analysis, implementation, test, and review stages
Run independent subtasks in isolated Git worktrees with pause, resume, retry, cancel, and rollback
Add a verification runner for build, unit tests, dev server, browser interactions, screenshots, and regression checks
Provide granular approval policies for file writes, shell commands, network access, and destructive operations
Persist sessions, artifacts, diffs, approvals, and verification results for restart and audit
Expose an extensibility layer for skills, hooks, MCP-style tools, and project instructions
Keep native UI responsive under high-volume streaming output and parallel task updates
safety_requirements: No writes outside the selected workspace or task worktree without approval
Complete audit trail for agent actions
Graceful cancellation and cleanup of child processes
